Each sub buffer has a pointer to its ""tail"" (the last event written to the

incremented to cover the size of the new event. This is done in a way that

the next sub buffer takes place. After setting the current sub buffer to

column2: the previous one that had the tail go passed the end of the

column1: sub buffer needs to be reset back to the original tail location (before
the new event was requested) and the rest of the sub buffer needs to be

The race happens when a reader takes control of the sub buffer. As readers
do a ""swap"" of sub buffers from the ring buffer to get exclusive access to
the sub buffer
column2: it replaces the ""head"" sub buffer with an empty sub buffer

column1: that goes back into the writable portion of the ring buffer. This swap can
happen as soon as the writer moves to the next sub buffer and before it
updates the last sub buffer with padding.
Because the sub buffer can be released to the reader while the writer is
still updating the padding
column2: it is possible for the reader to see the event

column1: that goes past the end of the sub buffer. This can cause obvious issues.
To fix this
column2: add a few memory barriers so that the reader definitely sees

column1: the updates to the sub buffer
column2: and also waits until the writer has put

column1: back the ""tail"" of the sub buffer back to the last event that was written
on it.
To be paranoid

column1: warn and shutdown the ring buffer code. 1 second should be enough as
the writer does have preemption disabled. If the writer doesn't move
